title: RegimeLab
subtitle: Forecasting, uncertainty and adaptation when the data changes.

cases.label: Stable regime
cases.title: A forecast is only useful out of sample.
cases.description: Predict next-day realized variance from six causal return features. Compare a small neural network, regularized regression, persistence and an expanding-window adaptation under a controlled volatility shock.

charts.title: Held-out realized variance and frozen prediction interval · every third target

method: Seed 73: Gaussian innovations with v[t]=ω+α r[t−1]²+β v[t−1]. Baseline (ω,α,β)=(0.025,0.10,0.84); from day 1450 the stress case uses (0.12,0.16,0.84), deliberately α+β=1. Features at close t: squared return, 5/20-day variance, return, 20-day mean absolute return and 5-day mean return. Label: r² at t+1.

Training targets <1000; validation 1001–1199 chooses ridge penalty 0.01; calibration 1201–1449 sets a finite-sample absolute-residual quantile; test starts 1451. Scaling is fitted on training only. Embargoed boundaries prevent target overlap.
A 6→12→1 tanh MLP trains for 350 full-batch epochs on log1p variance, with fixed settings and training-only normalization. No claim that this architecture is optimal is made.

Frozen ridge interval radius = 0.860936; lower endpoint clipped at zero. Expanding ridge refits every 60 targets, uses only earlier observed labels and keeps the previously selected penalty. It does not reuse the frozen interval as an adaptive guarantee.
limitations: Synthetic heteroscedastic data tests a known mechanism; it is not a historical market backtest or evidence of alpha. Squared returns are noisy variance proxies.
The post-break stress has unit variance persistence and no finite stationary unconditional variance. It is a deliberately nonstationary stress, not a stable high-volatility regime.
Serial dependence and deliberate distribution shift violate exchangeability. Split-conformal intervals here are diagnostics; 90% empirical coverage is not guaranteed under these conditions.
Mean absolute error, RMSE and QLIKE can rank models differently. QLIKE uses a 10⁻⁵ positivity floor, disclosed because near-zero forecasts can dominate it.
This trajectory shows one process seed; the repeated-seed cases quantify variability for the same generator. Shift mechanisms, model families and transaction costs are not explored.

cases.label: Repeated seeds / stable
cases.title: Does the conclusion survive a new process seed?
cases.description: Repeat all five forecasts on independent synthetic histories. Compare paired errors and frozen 90% interval coverage; each dataset has equal weight. Table coverage is a fraction; chart coverage is percent.

charts.title: Frozen interval coverage across process seeds

method: Process seeds: 100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119; 2,000 returns each. Stable/stress histories share innovations within each seed; independent streams across seeds. Seed 73 remains a separate illustrative trajectory.

Unchanged six causal features and train <1000, validation 1001-1199, calibration 1201-1449, test 1451-1999 (549 targets). Same Gaussian GARCH-like generator and day-1450 persistent stress as the trajectory cases.

Fixed grid [0.01, 1, 10, 100]; validation MSE selects within each dataset; first minimum wins. No test tuning or seed exclusion. Selected penalty frozen for all expanding refits. MLP settings and initialization seed fixed.

Equal weight per independent process seed. Sample SD (ddof=1), MCSE of mean = SD/sqrt(n), linear empirical p10/p90. Quantiles describe dataset variability, not confidence or prediction intervals. Regimes paired by innovations; days are not independent replicates.

Frozen ridge uses absolute calibration residuals at rank ceil((249+1)*0.9)=225; lower endpoint clipped at zero. Width is actual mean upper minus lower. Expanding ridge refits every 60 labels strictly before each forecast block, including earlier evaluation observations; its intervals are not assessed.

Paired table differences subtract the named baseline on the same seed; negative means lower error. QLIKE floor remains 1e-5. Per-seed scores, floor-hit fractions, alpha counts and paired coverage changes are in the study JSON.
Selected alpha frequencies: {'0.01': 3, '1': 1, '10': 2, '100': 14}
limitations: Twenty synthetic histories from one generator and one shift mechanism do not establish real-world forecasting accuracy or market edge. Local CPU/NumPy only; runtime, energy and monetary cost are unmeasured.

Fixed neural initialization isolates process variability; optimizer-seed variability and architecture search are not measured. These summaries evaluate the fixed selection procedure, not a single universal penalty.
Serial dependence and shift violate ordinary split-conformal exchangeability. Coverage is empirical, not a guaranteed 90%. Stress has alpha+beta=1 and no finite stationary unconditional variance.

Heavy-tailed seed errors and near-zero forecasts can dominate means and QLIKE. SD/MCSE and empirical quantiles from a small ensemble do not justify normal-theory significance claims. Regimes are paired, not 40 independent datasets.

cases.label: Feature ablation / stable
cases.title: Which information does the variance forecast need?
cases.description: Remove one causal feature group at a time and refit ridge. Compare full ridge, training mean and a validation-selected variant on separate test targets. Table coverage is a fraction; negative paired errors favor removal.

method: Process seeds 200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216, 217, 218, 219; 2,000 synthetic returns each. Disjoint from earlier seed-73 and seeds-100-119 studies; all paths retained.

Training targets <1000 (979); validation 1001-1199 (199); calibration 1201-1449 (249); test 1451-1999 (549). Boundaries 1000/1200/1450 excluded. Same Gaussian GARCH-like generator; stress starts day 1450 with alpha+beta=1.

Remove latest shock: latest squared return (column 0). Remove smoothed magnitude: 5/20-day realized variance and 20-day mean absolute return (1,2,4). Remove signed returns: latest return and 5-day mean return (3,5). Full ridge uses all six columns. Removals are separate, not cumulative; refitting estimates conditional predictive value, not a causal intervention.

Four fixed feature variants; alpha grid [0.01, 1, 10, 100]. Training-only scaling and coefficients. Validation MSE selects alpha separately per variant, then selects a variant. First minimum wins, full ridge first. Calibration sets each frozen model's 90% residual radius; test only scores. No test ranking selects a deployed variant; no refits or seed exclusions.

Equal weight per process seed; stable/stress share innovations. Sample SD (ddof=1), MCSE=SD/sqrt(n), linear empirical p10/p90 and range. Paired differences subtract full ridge within seed; lower_count counts negative differences (lower coverage is a failure, not a win).

Calibration rank is ceil((249+1)*0.9)=225, with lower endpoints clipped at zero. Training mean is a feature-free control calibrated separately. QLIKE floor is 1e-5; floor fractions, all validation scores, chosen alphas, seed-level results and selection counts are exported in study JSON.
Validation selection counts: {'Full ridge': 3, 'Without latest shock': 4, 'Without smoothed magnitude': 1, 'Without signed returns': 12}

Recorded isolation audit (stable seed 200): test-feature selection unchanged=True, test-target selection unchanged=True; maximum radius changes 0 / 0. Changing excluded boundary rows leaves the entire record unchanged=True. Calibration-target changes affect radii while test point errors stay fixed. Exact target ranges and intervention measurements are in the JSON export. These checks diagnose this implementation; they do not prove data provenance.
limitations: Synthetic data and one shift mechanism; this is no evidence of market accuracy. No neural or likelihood-objective ablation is included. Local CPU/NumPy; runtime, energy and monetary costs unmeasured.

Correlated magnitude features can substitute for each other. Removing a group with penalty reselection measures this training procedure's predictive dependence, not unique feature importance or a causal effect.

Selecting a variant increases validation reuse and can overfit its 199 targets. Test comparisons are descriptive; selecting a new winner from them would require fresh confirmation data. No significance claim or universal best subset is made.

Serial dependence and nonstationary stress invalidate ordinary exchangeable split-conformal guarantees. Coverage is empirical. Seed summaries have limited tail resolution; near-zero predictions can dominate QLIKE.

isolation_audit.scope: First listed process seed, stable history; deterministic row perturbations, not independent datasets.
